title: Natural Rate of Interest, Monetary Policy and Shocks in Tunisia
content: This paper estimates the natural rate of interest (r∗) for Tunisia from 1989Q1 to 2023Q4, applying the semi-structural model of Holston, Laubach, and Williams (2017) with adjustments to account for the COVID-19 pandemic. Our empirical results reveal a pronounced downward trend in r∗, which fell from approximately 2.9% in the early 1990s to 0.8% by 2023. This decline is driven by a sharp drop in potential Gross Domestic Product growth and is further validated by its consistency with the evolution of fundamental national accounts, where we document a synchronized secular decline in national savings and investment rates. Using r∗ as a benchmark, we compute the interest rate gap to characterize the monetary policy stance. The analysis identifies a restrictive policy period from 1989 to 2002 and a prolonged accommodative period from 2003 to 2023. These policy phases are empirically consistent with the evolution of key macroeconomic variables: the restrictive period coincided with a negative output gap and disinflation, while the accommodative period aligned with a positive output gap and rising inflation. Our findings underscore the challenges for monetary policy in a context of structurally declining growth potential.
